TraceAnalysis: The incident root cause is identified as mobservice1, which is generating excessive latency in calls to redisservice2. All 13 traces show isolated calls to redisservice2 with durations exceeding normal limits by 4-10 ms, reaching up to 29 seconds, and no upstream service involvement. This pattern confirms mobservice1 as the source of the performance degradation.
MetricAnalysis: Metric Expert Report: The production incident was caused by mobservice1 experiencing significant CPU overload on 2021/07/06 at 00:03:42. Multiple CPU metrics across different cores exhibited anomalies including sustained level shifts and transient spikes. These simultaneous anomalies across multiple cores indicate a system-wide CPU resource exhaustion. The severity of deviation from baseline metrics demonstrates critical performance degradation that impacted overall service availability.
LogAnalysis: The incident was caused by a failure in mobservice1, which triggered cascading issues across dependent services. At 2021-07-06 00:11, mobservice1 became unresponsive, leading to NullPointerExceptions in user-service during API processing due to unhandled null responses. Concurrently, order-service experienced DatabaseConnectionTimeoutExceptions from connection pool exhaustion, while payment-service encountered ServiceUnavailableException errors. The root cause was mobservice1's degradation, which propagated to critical downstream systems.
RootCauseAnalysis: The root cause of the incident was mobservice1 terminating unexpectedly. Evidence confirms the service transitioned to a "Finished" state prematurely, halting request processing. This ungraceful shutdown directly triggered service unavailability and cascading failures.
